page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 server family. It features 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The underlying hardware is powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of a 32 KB L1 data cache, a 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place the n2-standard-8 primarily in the average performance tier for standard operations, with some notable limitations in highly parallelized or specialized workloads. The instance achieves average ratings in multi-core CPU stress tests, memory bandwidth (measuring 50.27 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 37.18 GB/sec for uncached large block writes), and software compilation tasks. However, it exhibits weaker performance, falling into the bottom 25%, for single-core stress-ng tests, multi-core Geekbench scores, and specialized tasks such as ray tracing and image processing. LLM inference speeds for text generation using a small 135M model are average at 113.19 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for the same model is weak at 340.65 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for mainstream enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware. Given its average performance in database operations, static web serving throughput (6.9 GB/sec), and text processing, this instance is best suited for general-purpose applications. These include standard web servers, software compilation pipelines, and moderate database workloads that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
